scispace.query: Which rigorous results on polynomial matrix-function evaluation, minimal-polynomial quotient algebras, certified homotopy continuation and parallel-in-time integrators give explicit operation-count or critical-path complexity improvements while retaining a posteriori global error bounds for stiff ordinary differential equations?

Brehard, rigorous polynomial approximations thesis, tel-02337901
Sastre and Ibanez, matrix polynomial evaluation, doi:10.3390/math9141600
scispace.authority: No theorem or performance claim is accepted from the discovery summaries alone.

sources.title: Certified homotopy tracking using the Krawczyk method
sources.read_scope: Introduction and sections 2.2 and 3.2; Theorems2.1/3.1; algorithm assumptions and finite-precision caveat
sources.supports: Interval boxes can certify a unique root for every parameter in a window; endpoint-near-a-root alone does not establish path identity.
sources.limits: Does not prove VigilODE speed. The paper's analyzed exact-real affine parameter setting is not a complete binary64 certificate. Our exactly causal and nearcausal specializations are proved separately.

sources.title: Robust certified numerical homotopy tracking
sources.supports: Certified algebraic continuation has condition-dependent bit complexity.
sources.limits: No full-text theorem imported, no universal parallel speed inference.

sources.authors: Fatima Boudaoud; Fabrizio Caruso; Marie-Francoise Roy
sources.title: Certificates of Positivity in the Bernstein Basis
sources.read_scope: Publisher metadata and abstract only; full text paywalled
sources.supports: Bernstein positivity certificates are established literature.
sources.limits: Our multivariate matrix box bound follows from the explicitly proved partition-of-unity argument. Do not import the paper's univariate bit-complexity result into arbitrary-dimensional matrix compilation.

sources.title: Classical Orthogonal Polynomials, Generating Functions
sources.supports: Standard Laguerre normalization and family definitions.
sources.limits: The generating function does not supply an implementation total-error or speed certificate.

sources.title: What Is the Minimal Polynomial of a Matrix?
sources.read_scope: Author exposition, definitions, divisibility and Jordan multiplicities
sources.supports: Known annihilating-polynomial and matrix-function foundations; one must retain Jordan multiplicity.
sources.limits: No claim that a low-degree polynomial can be cheaply recovered from a generic black-box operator.
